```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

researchR is an R client for a separately deployed researchD server. The server
collects literature and signals; this package configures surveillance questions
and reads the stored results. It does not run a literature search locally.

## Install and connect

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("CTTIR/researchR", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

For a real server, configure `RESEARCHR_URL` and `RESEARCHR_TOKEN` privately.
The token must match the server's API token. The browser dashboard has a separate
login; its session is not an API credential. Do not put real tokens in scripts,
reports, screenshots or version control.

The following example runs entirely offline. It uses a reserved example URL and
a deliberately invalid demonstration token. `check = FALSE` prevents the
connection constructor from contacting a server; the default `check = TRUE`
requests server metadata immediately.

```{r offline-connection}
library(researchR)
conn <- rr_connect(
  base_url = "https://feeds.example.org",
  token = "demonstration-token-not-valid",
  check = FALSE
)
conn
```

## Describe a question

Terms within a concept are alternatives (OR); separate concepts are combined
with AND. Constructing a concept only creates an R object.

```{r concepts}
concepts <- list(
  rr_concept("exposure", terms = c("exercise", "physical activity")),
  rr_concept("outcome", terms = c("fatigue", "tiredness"))
)
concepts
```

On a configured server, the following call creates or updates the named question.
An update replaces its concept list, so supply the complete intended definition.
This example is not evaluated while building the documentation. Email delivery
is disabled explicitly.

```{r save-question, eval=FALSE}
live <- rr_connect()
rr_upsert_question(
  live, "exercise_fatigue", "Exercise and fatigue",
  concepts = concepts,
  sources = list(pubmed = TRUE, europepmc = TRUE),
  from_days_back = 14,
  email_enabled = FALSE
)
```

## Read stored results

These operations require your configured server and are not evaluated here.
Reading stored records does not trigger a new collection run. A working server
connection does not establish that every upstream source is healthy.

```{r read-results, eval=FALSE}
rr_questions(live)
records <- rr_records(live, "exercise_fatigue")
signals <- rr_signals(live, "exercise_fatigue")
rr_source_health(live)
rr_heartbeat(live)
```

Records and signals are returned as tibbles. Their contents depend on the
server's collection history and vocabulary; inspect `rr_meta(live)` after a
server upgrade. Empty results can mean that no records match or that collection
has not yet completed. They are not evidence that the literature is absent.
Empty responses preserve the same column types as populated results. Timestamp
columns use UTC and honor offsets supplied by the server; record `provenance` and
signal `extra` fields are list columns. A change detected while fetching pages
raises `researchR_pagination_changed`; retry once collection finishes.
Malformed API responses or structured metadata raise `researchR_protocol_error`
instead of implying that the search or metadata is empty. Request errors redact
submitted API keys and the bearer token; still remove credentials before sharing
diagnostics or a reproducible example.

## Construct feed URLs

Feed URL construction is local and does not contact the server. The default
feed follows the question's curated selection; `all = TRUE` removes the score
threshold. Every RSS feed is still capped by the server's `FEED_LIMIT`; use
`rr_records()` for all retained records. Feed URLs contain no API token, and
published feeds are open.

```{r feeds}
rr_feed_url(conn, "exercise_fatigue")
rr_feed_url(conn, "exercise_fatigue", all = TRUE)
rr_feed_url(conn, "exercise_fatigue", signals = TRUE)
```

Generating a URL does not verify that the corresponding question or feed exists.
Use the API for private management, and review the server's feed publication
settings before exposing a surveillance question.

## Reference and support

Use `help(package = "researchR")` for function contracts and
`citation("researchR")` for the installed version's citation. Report reproducible
problems at <https://github.com/CTTIR/researchR/issues>, with synthetic examples
and credentials removed. researchR is distributed under the MIT license.
